name: Read an analog clock instantly
blurb: Instant, not calculated. If you still work out "the big hand is on the seven, so that is 35", a few days of drilling replaces arithmetic with recognition.
gear: A clock-drill app or a printed worksheet
steps: Learn the twelve hour positions as shapes rather than numbers, so a hand position reads directly as a time.
Learn the five-minute marks as positions, not multiplications: the three position is 15, the six is 30, the nine is 45.
Learn to read the minute hand’s fine position between marks by eye.
Drill with random times, aiming to answer in under a second.
Practise on clocks with no numerals, and on Roman-numeral faces, which break the counting habit.
Wear an analogue watch for a fortnight so you get dozens of unconscious reps a day.
tips: The hour hand also moves. At half past, it sits between two numerals — reading it as the earlier hour is the classic error.
Roman IIII on watch faces is traditional, not a mistake.
proof: You read any analogue clock correctly, including numeral-free faces, in under a second.
